title: Green Growth and Emerging Markets: How Does It Affect Leading Companies in the Stock Market?
content: The transition to green growth models imposes adaptation costs on firms that may affect their performance in stock markets; however, evidence for emerging markets is scarce. This study analyzes the relationship between green growth, measured by the Green Growth Index (GGI), and stock market returns in a panel of 16 emerging markets during the 2010-2024 period. Using a two-way fixed-effects model with standard error to robust heteroscedasticity and autocorrelation, and controlling for GDP growth and inflation, we find that a one-point increase in the GGI is associated with a 5.17 percentage point decrease in the annual return of a country’s main stock market index in the same year. This negative and statistically significant relationship is robust to the exclusion of countries with outliers and to the use of the GGI at levels rather than first differences. The findings are consistent with transition cost arguments and with the documented short-term negative effects observed in European markets. The study contributes to the literature by employing the GGI in a panel of emerging markets under a two-way fixed-effects specification.
